text.p: Pakistan and India on Tuesday released hundreds of each other's fishermen detained for three to four years for alleged illegal fishing in the other country's territorial waters, Pakistani officials said.

Pakistan released 193 Indian fishermen in the port city of Karachi, and the official APP news agency quoted officials as saying 94 Pakistani fishermen were simultaneously freed in India under an accord reached between the two sides in June.
The Indians, most of them from the western state of Gujarat, were driven from Karachi's Landhi Jail in four police vans to the airport to board a special Indian Airlines flight to Bombay.

The Pakistani fishermen released in India will be flown to Karachi from Bombay by a special Pakistan International Airlines flight on Wednesday, Pakistani officials said. The release of the detained fishermen was undertaken after Pakistani and Indian foreign ministry secretaries reached an agreement during a meeting in Islamabad last month, which also provided for the return of the seized fishing boats.
Indian diplomats told reporters in Karachi that apart from some problems, arrangements by Pakistani officials during the repatriation process were satisfactory.

"We believe there are more Indians in Pakistani jails," an Indian diplomat, N.K. Chopra, said. "It has been decided by both sides that immediately after they are identified, they will also be repatriated from both the sides," he said.

The president of the Fishermen's Society in Gujarat, Veliji Masani, said the crew from both sides of the border are either lured by bigger catch or by strong currents into territorial waters of each other.
He said this was the first repatriation after about 80 fishermen were exchanged in 1994.
One of the freed Indian fisherman, Jaintee (one name), said he was arrested by Pakistani Coast Guards in November 1994.
"We were very pleased when we read in newspapers that Indian and Pakistani officials, in their meeting in Islamabad, have decided to repatriate us," he said.
Another fisherman, Nago Jee, said more than 25 Indians were still in the Landhi Jail.

Early this year, Pakistan repatriated 38 Indian children held with adult fishermen as a goodwill gesture before the Indian and Pakistani officials resumed peace talks between in March in New Delhi after a three-year hiatus.
